counterexample: Conforming-alternative challenge: an implementation using a vanilla JavaScript frontend, different control labels and different save API routes still fits integration.md:3 and policy.md:5. Failing this row merely for the runtime paths or package names would falsely reject that permitted product request; the full reading does not do so. False-pass challenge: a prompt could start with the exact friendly first sentence and then append a numbered acceptance matrix or a React/file/endpoint construction recipe. Reviewing only line 1 would miss that defect. Reading all five main paragraphs and all six notes found no such appended recipe here. Broken-app boundary: a static mock with inert Run and Save controls would not fulfill instruction.md:1,3,7, but a natural-language-row Pass would not establish that mock's correctness. App execution is outside this row; no successful runtime is inferred from the prose.
